Translation: A worker's Energy affects their Productivity. Tired workers get less done.
Oversee Work to boost your workers' Productivity.
Workers with low Opinion of you may decide to leave.
Workers are better at different things. Match their Skills to the task to get the most out of them.
Visit a Guild House to train in your profession or unlock a new one.
Keep your buildings in good repair. Low Integrity can affect several aspects of your business.
Upgrades transform the building itself, changing its appearance and unlocking major new features. Improvements are smaller additions that provide extra benefits.
Sell goods from your Storefront, or take them to the Marketplace by cart.
Better Carts can carry more goods, travel faster, and withstand more damage.
Escort valuable carts if you would rather your profits reach their destination.
The Marketplace offers variety, but other businesses and Resource Sites may offer better deals.
Raw materials are often cheapest when bought directly from Resource Sites.
Your Personal Inventory holds items you can use or equip, but those items cannot be traded normally.
Prices change with supply, demand, seasons, laws, and events in the wider world.
Taxes are collected at the end of the year. Prosperity has its traditions.
Check your end-of-year balance before taxes turn success into imprisonment.
Explore the city and see what its buildings have to offer. Useful actions and opportunities may be hiding in plain sight.
Hover over highlighted terms and icons to learn more about them.
Press the middle mouse button to lock a tooltip in place.
Locked tooltips are interactive; hover over their highlighted terms to dig deeper.
Spammed your screen with tooltips? Left-click to dismiss them all.
Left-click an item or worker to pick them up, then left-click again to place them.
Click to pick up, click to drop — it works for both items and workers.
Right-click while moving an item or worker to return them to where they started.
Double-click an item stack to pick up the whole stack. Or click and drag to choose an exact amount.
To pick items from a stack one by one, click at intervals. Double-click to pick up the entire stack.
Press Esc to close the most recently opened window. If no windows are open, Esc opens the pause menu.
Building and Marketplace screens can be moved by dragging them from the top.
Right-click a character or item to open a menu of things you can do with them.
Click a character to view their details.
Right-click inside a window to close the topmost window.
The shortcuts for closing all windows and opening the Pause Menu can be changed in Settings.
You can enter a building just by double-clicking it.
Right-click to exit a building.
Hold Alt to highlight all buildings and interactive objects.
A lasting Dynasty needs someone to inherit what you have built.
Age, Health, Wealth, Traits and Skills can all matter when choosing a spouse.
Gifts and sweet-talking can speed up a courtship before another suitor gets there first.
A successful courtship is followed by a wedding on the next turn.
Name an eligible heir if you do not trust the default line of succession.
Train your future heir early. Death rarely waits for convenient succession planning.
Introduce family members to your Guild to prepare them for the profession, then put them in charge of your businesses as Masters.
Click a dynasty crest to open its Family screen and view the full family tree.
Check the Lawbook before getting creative. Laws determine which actions are crimes.
Evidence can be used to press charges or as leverage against other citizens.
A jury that likes you is generally preferable to one that does not.
The severity of a crime determines how unpleasant the punishment may become.
Political offices offer both influence over the city and a respectable salary.
Wealth and Title open the way to higher political positions.
Good Rhetoric and the appointers' Opinion can help win an election.
While in office, you can use the city treasury to improve Districts and Quarters.
Some offices let you change which actions are crimes and how severely they are punished.
